did_you_know.text: Did you know? David came to Nob alone, and Ahimelech the priest was alarmed when he saw him and asked why no one was with him.
Did you know? David explained to Ahimelech that the king had sent him on a secret mission, and that no one was to know anything about it.
Did you know? David asked Ahimelech for five loaves of bread, or whatever bread he had available.
Did you know? Ahimelech replied that he had no ordinary bread, only consecrated bread, and said he would give it to them only if the young men had kept themselves from women.
Did you know? David said that the young men were pure in this regard, and also claimed that their equipment was consecrated and that they were on an urgent mission.
Did you know? The priest gave David the consecrated bread, after the bread had been removed from before the LORD and replaced with hot bread on the day it was taken away.
Did you know? Doeg the Edomite, one of Saul’s servants and the chief of his herdsmen, was there before the LORD that day and saw what happened.
Did you know? When David asked for a weapon, Ahimelech offered him the sword of Goliath the Philistine, which was wrapped up and kept behind the ephod.
Did you know? David took Goliath’s sword and fled from Saul that same day to Achish, king of Gath.
Did you know? Achish’s servants recognized David and recalled the song: “Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands.”
Did you know? After David heard what Achish’s servants said, he became very afraid of Achish, king of Gath, and changed his behavior in front of the Philistines.
Did you know? Achish rejected David, saying that he had no need of a madman in his household; thus the encounter ended without Achish harming him.
